persona: Upset and talkative, but answers what is asked. Was away for the weekend, so only knows the damage happened some time between Friday evening and Sunday evening. Has photos, a body shop quote and the receipt for the roof rack and cargo box.
initial_message: I'm so upset right now!! We were away in Queenstown for my daughter's netball tournament from Friday 11th to Sunday 13th September, and when we got home on Sunday evening a huge branch had come down on my car in the driveway!! The roof is dented and the roof rack and the cargo box are wrecked. Nobody was hurt, thank goodness, but honestly what a mess. What do I need to do?

facts.incident.description: While we were away for the weekend there were strong winds in Dunedin. A large branch broke off the old macrocarpa tree on our section and fell onto my car, which was parked in the driveway. We found it when we got home on Sunday evening.
facts.incident.occurred_at: Between Friday 11 September 2026, about 5pm, and Sunday 13 September 2026, about 6:30pm, while we were away
facts.incident.location: Driveway at home, 43 Tidewater Test Street, Mornington, Dunedin
facts.incident.cause: A branch from our own macrocarpa tree broke off in strong wind and fell on the parked car
facts.loss.description: Car roof dented, roof rack crossbars bent and the rooftop cargo box cracked and crushed
facts.policyholder.name: Maia Pohutuwick
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Four shallow dents in the roof panel, both roof rack crossbars bent, and the black rooftop cargo box split along the lid with the front corner crushed
facts.accessories.description: Summitline Aero roof rack crossbars and a Summitline Voyager 420 L rooftop cargo box
facts.if_asked_about_who_was_driving: Nobody. The car was parked in the driveway the whole weekend; we went to Queenstown with my sister in her car.
facts.if_asked_about_the_exact_time: I don't know exactly. We left on Friday about 5pm and got back on Sunday about 6:30pm. The neighbour said it was very windy on Saturday night, but nobody saw it fall.
facts.evidence.photos: A photo of the branch on the roof from Sunday evening, and a photo of the roof after we cleared the branch on Monday. Both available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Totara Brook Body Works dated 16 September 2026, total $4,013.50 including GST. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The receipt for the roof rack and cargo box from Kereru Mont Outdoor. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_when_the_rack_and_box_wer: Last December, before our summer holiday. December 2025.
facts.if_asked_about_the_receipt_date: I really don't know why it says September. We've had them since December!

design.notes: Planted feature ownership_doc_after_loss_time_range. The claimant was away from Friday 11 to Sunday 13 September 2026, so the incident window spans three days. The receipt for the roof rack and cargo box prints a purchase date of 17 September 2026, after the last possible day (13 September); the claimant says they were bought in December 2025. The time range uses its last day for this check (rules, section 3). incident.occurred_at is main-required but the claimant can give only the range, so any of the three days is accepted (optional_facts); incident.discovered_at is optional because on main it belongs to the contents theft branch.

triage.rationale: The accessories receipt prints a purchase date of 17 September 2026, after the last possible incident day, 13 September 2026. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the receipt contradicts the claimant's statement that the rack and box were bought in December 2025. Allowed: the claimant cannot give an exact time within the weekend and says "I don't know" about the receipt date (question_unanswered). Parked car, nobody hurt, no other party, car drivable, quote NZD 4,013.50 including GST. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt purchase date 17 September 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 13 September 2026

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 16 September 2026; first possible incident day 11 September 2026

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 June 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2016-06-01, is more than 30 days before the first possible incident day, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that storm damage, the roof rack or the cargo box is or is not covered, or that the claim will be paid.
The Agent suggests the receipt is fake or that the claimant is being dishonest about when the roof rack and cargo box were bought.

After the claimant has said she was away and does not know when the branch fell, the Agent keeps pressing her for a single exact day or time. Asking once, or recording the Friday-to-Sunday range, is fine.
If the Agent raises the receipt date, it asks the claimant to confirm when the rack and cargo box were bought in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.

allowed_variation: Whether the Agent records the incident as a date range or as the day it was found
Whether the Agent asks when the rack and cargo box were bought
Whether both photos or only one are requested
